status: Canonical plan adopted from visible AAE-R1B R3(iv), R4 and R5; no lesson counts as shipped until built, gated and merged.
subject: AAE-R1B: fourteen new GROW Art Silver decks from SPEC.json. Two units remain separately evidenced; full 1C and1D decks, all nine parts covered. Week distribution and theme are implementation choices.

slotsSource.status: All slot entries are empty and candidate arrangements unconfirmed at this source snapshot.

theme: Arts Practice, Pathways And Leadership (implementation choice)

level.title: Level 2 Award in the Arts

1A.name: Plan an arts challenge
1A.requires: own strengths and weaknesses; an own action plan
1A.note: The challenge must NOT focus on leadership. The adviser must not write the plan.

1B.name: Implement and review the arts challenge
1B.requires: ongoing evidence; someone ELSE's review of the challenge; the pupil's own final review

1C.name: Review arts events
1C.requires: at least one event or experience attended AS AN AUDIENCE MEMBER; a review of artistic qualities and creative impact; the review SHARED, evidenced

1D.name: Arts research
1D.requires: MEET arts practitioners and gain first-hand experience through workshops or events; research arts organisations; education AND career pathways; a summary in the pupil's own words of the influence

2A.name: Plan the project and own leadership role

2B.name: Plan practical issues
2B.requires: promotion, recruitment, resources, risk, feedback plan

level.attemptedRule: ONE Attempted allowed PER UNIT. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass.

rows.title: Choose My Arts Challenge
rows.outcome: Use the pupil’s actual work to identify their own strengths and weaknesses. Try or compare feasible arts skills and choose a personal arts-development challenge with a reason. Keep the baseline and pupil’s choice. The challenge must not focus on leadership.

rows.title: Make My Own Action Plan
rows.outcome: Teach how to connect an arts aim to practical steps, resources, support, times and progress checks. The pupil writes, records or dictates their own action plan and tests whether its steps meet their chosen challenge. Staff may prompt or scribe exactly; they must not write the plan.

rows.title: Try, Record And Refine
rows.outcome: Teach a useful arts technique or method appropriate to the pupil’s challenge, then undertake real practice. Preserve baseline and changing states before revision, record what was done and adapt the next step. Start a sustained process record. An informal outside view here does not replace the later required review of the challenge.

rows.title: Experience, Review And Share
rows.outcome: A full Unit 1C deck: prepare focused audience questions, attend an actual arts event or experience as an audience member, review its artistic qualities and creative impact in the pupil’s own words, then actually share the review with another person. Record who received it, how it was shared and the exact evidence location. Label preparation, attendance, review and final sharing distinctly; a draft swap alone is not the completed sharing step. The genuine experience may use programme time beyond this lesson spine.
experiencePhases: own review of artistic qualities and creative impact

rows.title: Meet A Practitioner And Trace A Path
rows.outcome: A full Unit 1D deck: prepare pupil questions, meet arts practitioners and gain first-hand experience through workshops or events, research arts organisations, investigate education AND career pathways, and make an own-words summary of the influence. Keep actual first-hand findings distinct from source research. Read both shared slots; empty slots allow labelled preparation, never invented contact or completion. The genuine encounter may use programme time beyond this lesson spine.
experiencePhases: actual practitioner meeting and first-hand workshop or event

rows.title: Compare The Reviews And Judge Progress
rows.outcome: Complete a meaningful phase of real arts-challenge practice. Gather someone ELSE’s review of the challenge and the pupil’s own FINAL review, using the aim, actual process, outcomes and outside view. Record the identity or role of the other reviewer and the location of their real review. An adult model or generic checklist tick is not either required review.

rows.title: Plan My Arts Project And Role
rows.outcome: Begin the separately evidenced Arts leadership unit. Compare practical arts-project options, choose a project and define the pupil’s own leadership role. Teach how to connect the purpose, intended outcomes, people and role. In a group project each pupil identifies their own responsibility. Do not impose a public showing as a Silver requirement.

rows.title: Make The Practical Plan
rows.outcome: Teach and make a practical plan for the chosen project covering promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and feedback. Use the real scale, people and setting to choose workable arrangements. The pupil makes the choices and records their own plan; no pre-written adult plan or invented receipt, signature or chart quota.

rows.title: Test The Plan With The Team
rows.outcome: Work with actual collaborators to test a project step or resource, listen to responses, agree roles and resolve a practical issue. Update the pupil’s practical plan and record their own contribution and response to others. This is actual preparation and working with others; rehearsal is labelled rehearsal and is not claimed as project delivery.

rows.title: Lead The Project In Action
rows.outcome: Deliver the planned arts project or a genuine phase with real participants. Show the pupil’s own leadership, communication, role and decisions, and how they work with others. Preserve actual responses and any safe changes made. A finished group product alone cannot identify the pupil’s contribution.

rows.title: Continue The Project And Adapt
rows.outcome: Support real project delivery at the scale and time the pupil planned. Teach how to use a genuine issue or response to adapt a task, resource, explanation or role and check its effect with others. Do not invent a second workshop or public event; these two delivery decks can support phases of one project. Keep actual role and collaboration evidence.

rows.title: Work Well With Others
rows.outcome: Carry out an actual remaining team task or project follow-up. Practise listening, agreeing an action, fulfilling the pupil’s role and checking the result with other people. Connect this new real collaboration to records gathered during preparation and delivery. A fictional disagreement exercise can model a method, but cannot replace working with others.

rows.title: Review My Leadership Project
rows.outcome: Make the pupil’s own leadership-project review from actual aims, role, practical decisions, delivery, work with others and feedback. Teach how to link a claim to an example and judge achievements and limits. The pupil chooses a reasoned next step. Staff may scribe exact words but must not write the review.

rows.title: Find The Evidence Across Both Units
rows.outcome: Complete or clarify the pupil’s own project review, then check existing evidence for all nine parts: 1A, 1B, 1C, 1D, 2A, 2B, 2C, 2D and 2E. Keep the two units separately identifiable and every part separately locatable. Check exact file-plus-page/slide/timecode locators and the twenty-file cap. Record genuine gaps and arrange completion; the audit does not teach or fabricate missing activities.

unitSeparation.1: Arts practice and pathways — rows 1–6; own arts challenge is not focused on leadership.
unitSeparation.2: Arts leadership — rows 7–14; separately identifiable project and personal leadership evidence.
unitSeparation.rule: Retain unit and part labels on all evidence and locators; do not treat Unit 2 as the challenge required by Unit 1A.

portfolio.format: digital, organised by unit and part
portfolio.suggestion: Nine cumulative part files, one per registered part, are a possible layout. Two unit files with clearly labelled part sections can also work. Neither layout is an award rule. Do not create a compulsory file for every lesson.
portfolio.locator: actual filename plus page, slide or timecode; every required item separately locatable
portfolio.attemptedRule: ONE Attempted allowed PER UNIT. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass.

staffRequirements: Name Silver and the actual unit and part(s) directly taught; distinguish final portfolio checks.
State the per-unit Attempted rule, any Not Attempted consequence, whole-Silver twenty-file cap and all four assessment areas.
Results are Pass / Below Pass. Only an adviser trained at Silver may assess; delivery is through a validated centre. State both as conditions staff must confirm, not as completed facts.
Advisers must not write pupil plans, reviews or evidence. Prompt, read or accurately scribe the pupil’s exact words and check them back.
Core / Extend / Challenge vary support within Silver. Every route retains the same required evidence and the pupil’s own choices, activity and review.
Teach the skill or method before independent evidence production. Keep adult models visibly separate from pupil work.
Use accessible tools and communication routes without forced personal disclosure, compulsory filming or public posting.

slotPolicy.runtime: The built serving decks must actually read the shared SLOTS mechanism; declarations alone do not demonstrate a working read.
slotPolicy.emptySlots: Author usable preparation and active-experience pathways now. No empty slot is treated as a booking, attendance, meeting or completed experience.
slotPolicy.noSubstitute: Desk research, archives and prerecorded video are labelled preparation and cannot replace the first-hand practitioner meeting.
slotPolicy.unit2Showing: No required SHOWING_SLOT and no imposed public showing. Add an optional slot declaration only if the chosen real project uses it.

hours.note: The lesson spine is nine hours twenty minutes, not the whole ninety-five-hour programme. Actual additional guided and independent practice, audience experience, practitioner contact and project delivery need to be arranged and recorded. Preparation-only sessions do not complete active evidence requirements.

cellsNote: Silver-specific GROW Art cell measurement has not been performed in this proposal. Leave cells unclaimed pending an independent measurement; neither Bronze nor Explore findings settle Silver. Do not invent or silently reassign workbook coverage.

secondaryPlacement.note: Catalogue or hub rows point at the same measured GROW deck; no second authored or re-banded copy. Follow the separate placement ordering required by the visible plan review.

reviewGates: Before authoring, root should remeasure the gate risks recorded in silver-plan-review.md; they are earlier diagnostics, not a claim about the current gate code.
Preserve the truthful Unit 1A restriction against leadership-focused challenges; do not delete it to evade a text selector.
Require a real final 1C review-sharing action and record of recipient, method and evidence location.
Require 1D full first-hand experience, organisation research, education AND career routes and own influence summary.
Final deck declares 2E directly, listsPortfolio true, and explicitly prints all nine part identifiers and their meanings.
Run actual GROW Art content and FK measurements, award gates and rendered/browser checks after authoring; structural review alone is not a PASS for the decks.

ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.issue: The original AAE-R1B order is not included verbatim in this delegated context.
ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.decision: Use the parent’s explicit constraints and the supplied review. Do not claim this sequence quotes an unseen week/medium clause. Root should reconcile any additional explicit order text before adoption.

ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.issue: No exact minimum number of practitioners, organisations, meetings or project events is provided in the Silver register wording.
ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.decision: Preserve the wording and required types of experience without adding a numeric quota. Ensure real practitioner meeting and first-hand workshop/event evidence; do not infer a number from plural nouns or another award level.

ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.issue: The supplied review suggests two cumulative unit files; part-level files may make locating nine parts easier.
ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.decision: Offer nine part files or two sectioned unit files as optional layouts within twenty total. Keep both units and all parts distinct in either layout.

ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.issue: The event, encounter and project do not naturally fit forty-minute sessions.
ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.decision: Keep full serving decks with explicit phases and actual extended programme time. Do not claim an unconfirmed experience happened or squeeze its evidence into a false timetable.

ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.issue: Rows for preparation and delivery can genuinely evidence both a practical/delivery part and working with others.
ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.decision: The proposal uses part for the primary code and parts for every directly evidenced part. Canonical consumers must preserve parts, or root should adopt an equivalent unambiguous representation; do not erase genuine multi-part teaching.

ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.issue: Some pupils may complete one project within a single delivery session.
ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.decision: Two delivery decks support a project’s actual phases, not a two-event award minimum. Adapt the timetable and use only real further delivery where needed.

ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.issue: GROW Art workbook cells have not been measured for Silver.
ambiguitiesAndConservativeDecisions.decision: Keep cells empty until measured. No secondary LAUNCH lesson units and no inherited Bronze or Explore claim.

cellPosition: No new cell claims: independent GROW Art review pending; a shared word is not a matching ruled outcome.
